rows.description: Parents say to buy gold and fixed deposits, which feels old-fashioned. Hear the caution and their memory of losses, but learn modern options and invest gradually. Neither blind trust nor dismissal serves you.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, envy, fear, guilt, loyalty, manipulation

rows.description: A friend asks you to bring in your savings for a scheme that pays referral bonuses. Loyalty does not mean joining. Tell them your concerns kindly, check regulators' warnings, and never recruit others into what you cannot verify.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, envy, fear, guilt, manipulation

rows.description: After losing savings on a hot tip, you feel stupid and hide it. Losses are common, and shame keeps people repeating them. Stop, review what happened, tell someone, and rebuild slowly with rules.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, envy, fear, loyalty, manipulation

rows.description: Your partner worries about your risky bets and hidden trades. Transparency about money is trust. Share holdings, agree on a limit for experimentation, and listen when they express fear rather than defending your ego.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, envy, guilt, loyalty, manipulation
related mind states: fear, anxiety, trust

rows.description: A caller posing as a bank or a job recruiter sounds friendly and urgent. Scams exploit trust and fear. Never share OTPs or pay upfront fees, verify through official numbers, and remember that anyone can be fooled.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, fear, indifference, shame
related mind states: fear, detachment, trust

rows.description: A message claims a digital arrest, parcel with drugs or legal action, demanding money now. Real agencies do not demand payment on video calls. Hang up, tell family, and report at 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, indifference, shame, trust

rows.description: After losing money, you feel too embarrassed to tell anyone. Shame is what scammers rely on. Report immediately to bank and cyber portal, since speed can recover funds, and share the story to protect others.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, fear, indifference, trust

rows.description: Rage at the fraudster is natural. Use it to file a proper complaint, gather screenshots and transaction IDs, and warn friends. Trying to hunt them yourself or scam them back is risky and rarely helps.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, fear, indifference, shame, trust

rows.description: Parents scold you after the loss, and you feel worse. Their anger is fear. Say you are already reporting it and ask for support instead of lectures, and help them learn safeguards too, since older relatives are also targets.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, fear, indifference, shame, trust
related mind states: anger, fear, trust

rows.description: A friend or an elderly relative has just been scammed. Do not blame or say I told you so. Help them stop further payment, report the incident, and rebuild confidence with clear safety habits.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, fear, indifference, shame, trust
